newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks fall in listless trading.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks fall in listless trading.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell Monday in a listless session that closely followed trading on Wall Street.
"We had a really slack day today, one of the worst in a long time, with scant turnover and not even much same-day buy-sell dealing," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 15.16 points at 3,760.55. Trading volume was lackluster at 61.3 million shares traded.
Analysts and dealers said the IPC rebounded from a session low of 3,735.98 points on last-minute bargain-hunting prompted by a recovery on Wall Street.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 20.02 at 6,955.48 points after falling as much as 80 points earlier in the session.
"What helped us was the (upward) adjustment in the Dow Jones and the price of U.S. long bonds," said Hector Jimenez, a technical analyst at the Inverlat brokerage in Mexico City.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond pared earlier losses and closed off 6/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
The broad market echoed the downward trend in blue chips. Out of a total of 95 stocks traded, sliders outnumbered gainers by 49 to 25.

Telecomms firm Telmex L shares, off four centavos (less than one cent) at 15.86 pesos ($1.99), weighed most heavily on the market, followed by retail stock Cifra C shares, which fell 22 centavos (three cents) to 10.84 pesos ($1.36).
Debt-ridden holding company Sidek headed the prominent gainers, up two centavos (less than one cent) to 46 centavos (six cents), on what dealers said was low-volume speculative buying.
Traders said other leading gainers and decliners were shares whose prices had moved in thin trading.
Dealers said stock prices would depend on the outlook for the government treasury bond auction set for Tuesday evening, and said they also awaited January industrial output figures.
"I think some are waiting for prices to fall further before buying. It seems that we have already gone on vacation," one trader said, referring to forthcoming pubic holidays.
